speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have knee pain after increasing your physical activity; to help me diagnose the specific cause, could you tell me exactly where on the knee the pain is located?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of repetitive pivoting and twisting in volleyball, do you hear a "popping" sound when the pain started, or does the knee feel unstable or give way when you try to walk or run?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splints)

The specific pain location over the medial tibia is classic for this condition, especially given your recent increase in volleyball activity; do you notice the pain worsening when you run or jump, and is it tender to the touch along the shin bone?
